stories.headline: Apple set to unveil Gemini-powered Siri reboot at WWDC after secret AI strategy meeting

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reported on June 7 that Apple's top executives, excluding Tim Cook, held a secret meeting in early 2025 to discuss how far behind it was in AI and chart a path forward — the results of which will be unveiled at WWDC on June 8.
key_facts.excerpt: The WWDC 2026 keynote is Tim Cook's last as Apple CEO — expect a defining statement on AI and software... Apple is set to announce a major Siri overhaul at the WWDC 2026 keynote, powered by Google's Gemini AI.

key_facts.fact: Apple is expected to rebuild Siri on a custom Google Gemini model under a multi-year partnership reportedly worth roughly $1 billion a year, arriving two years late after Apple settled a $250 million false-advertising lawsuit over the original 2024 promises.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple's WWDC 2026 developer conference, starting today at 10 a.m. PT at Apple Park in Cupertino, is set to unveil iOS 27 and a rebuilt Siri powered by a custom Google Gemini model costing roughly $1 billion a year. The same AI assistant overhaul Apple demonstrated at WWDC 2024, promoted in iPhone 16 advertising for months, and then settled a $250 million false-advertising lawsuit over is now two years late arriving.

key_facts.fact: iOS 27 will introduce a new Extensions framework that lets any AI chatbot installed from the App Store plug into Siri, Writing Tools and Image Playground — fine print in a pre-release build reads: 'Extensions allow agents from installed apps to work with Siri, the Siri app and other features on your devices.'
key_facts.excerpt: iOS 27 also introduces the Extensions framework, a system that lets any AI chatbot installed from the App Store plug directly into Siri and other Apple Intelligence surfaces, including Writing Tools and Image Playground. Fine print in a pre-release iOS 27 build, reported by Gurman, reads: "Extensions allow agents from installed apps to work with Siri, the Siri app and other features on your devices."

key_facts.fact: Siri will live within the iPhone's Dynamic Island as a glowing animation that expands into a translucent results card, with a standalone Siri app providing persistent conversation history, file uploads, and text-and-voice modes.
key_facts.excerpt: Activating the assistant produces a glowing animation in the Dynamic Island, the pill-shaped cutout at the top of the iPhone screen, which expands into a translucent results card that can be swiped into a full conversation view... A standalone Siri app with persistent conversation history, file and image uploads, and text-and-voice modes completes the redesign.

key_facts.fact: Apple Intelligence will expand into the Camera app with a Visual Intelligence mode powered by Google Image Search, and the Photos app is expected to gain AI editing tools including scene extension, object removal and natural-language edits.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple Intelligence also expands into the Camera app in iOS 27. A new Visual Intelligence mode, powered by Google Image Search, sits alongside Photo, Video, and Portrait in the camera carousel and can identify objects captured by the lens. The Photos app is expected to gain AI editing tools including scene extension, object removal, and natural-language edits.

stories.headline: Memory vendors say China's CXMT DDR5 is no bargain — prices match Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron

key_facts.fact: Memory module vendors at Computex 2026 told Wccftech that CXMT's DDR5 prices are 'almost on par' with Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron, debunking the assumption that the Chinese newcomer would crash consumer pricing
key_facts.excerpt: Multiple suppliers revealed that CXMT's memory is not cheap — its DDR5 solution pricing is virtually on par with Samsung, SK hynix, and Micron. CXMT's primary advantage is not price disruption but rather its relatively ample traditional DRAM production capacity.

key_facts.fact: CXMT's edge comes from supply, not price: since it does not prioritize HBM or SOCAMM for AI customers it has more traditional DRAM capacity available for client markets
key_facts.excerpt: ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) is gaining attention as a potential new force in the global DRAM market, but memory module vendors say the Chinese chipmaker is not offering the low-cost DDR5 supply many in the PC sector had hoped for.

key_facts.fact: CXMT also does not impose the supply penalties that Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron currently force on customers seeking additional allocation — making it an attractive secondary source despite matching prices
key_facts.excerpt: Multiple suppliers revealed that CXMT's memory is not cheap... CXMT's primary advantage is not price disruption but rather its relatively ample traditional DRAM production capacity. Since CXMT has not prioritized capacity allocation for AI customers, nor has it aggressively pursued advanced solutions such as HBM or SOCAMM, it has been able to maintain a foothold in the traditional DRAM supply market.

key_facts.fact: A Lexar regional manager warned at Computex that DRAM prices could double by year-end, with current channel discounts merely reflecting short-term inventory clearance
key_facts.excerpt: A Lexar regional manager warned at COMPUTEX that DRAM prices could double by year-end, with current channel discounts merely reflecting short-term inventory clearance.

stories.headline: UK, France, Germany back direct Zelensky-Putin ceasefire talks; Zelensky open to freezing front lines

key_facts.fact: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer, French President Emmanuel Macron and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky at 10 Downing Street on Sunday June 7 and issued a joint statement supporting direct dialogue between Ukraine and Russia, with active US and European participation, to bring about a ceasefire.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky received the backing of the leaders of the UK, France and Germany in calling for direct ceasefire talks between Russia and Ukraine, according to a joint statement issued following defence talks in London on Sunday. ... The leaders 'supported the proposal for a direct dialogue between Ukraine and Russia– with active US and European participation – to bring about a ceasefire and support further negotiations'.

key_facts.fact: In a Sky News interview, Zelensky said he would accept freezing the war along current front lines as the 'quickest way' to halt the fighting, while stressing it must lead to broader diplomatic talks to prevent renewed aggression.
key_facts.excerpt: 'Yes. It's the quickest way,' Zelensky replied. He stressed, however, that any freeze would need to be part of a broader diplomatic process aimed at preventing renewed aggression. 'We want to stop the war in a way where the war will not come back,' he said.

key_facts.fact: The leaders set five conditions for a 'just and lasting peace', starting with an immediate and complete ceasefire, the current line of contact as the starting point for talks, legally binding security guarantees for Ukraine including a multinational force, and keeping Russian assets frozen until Russia compensates Ukraine.
key_facts.excerpt: The European leaders and Zelenskiy set out the conditions that would need to be in place to secure a 'just and lasting peace', starting with an immediate and complete ceasefire. They said the current line of contact should be the starting point for talks, that Ukraine should have legally binding security guarantees, including the deployment of a multinational force, and that Russian assets would remain immobilised until Russia had compensated Ukraine for the damage caused by the war.

key_facts.fact: Putin rebuffed Zelensky's open-letter proposal for face-to-face talks, saying he saw 'no point' in such a meeting until a peace deal was agreed and insisting that any settlement would require Ukraine to surrender the entire Donetsk region.
key_facts.excerpt: In an open letter to Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday, Zelensky proposed they hold a face-to-face meeting. ... Putin Rules Out Meeting Zelensky and Vows to Pursue War Goals

key_facts.fact: Zelensky also told Starmer that Ukraine needed more missiles for air defence systems as Russia's war stretched into its fifth year, with daily strikes on Ukrainian energy and civilian infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: Mr Zelenskyy said in a post on X that he also told Starmer Ukraine needed more missiles for air defence systems, just days after he published an open letter to Putin proposing face-to-face talks about ending the war, now in its fifth year.

stories.headline: Factorial raises $150M Series D at $2.5B valuation for AI 'workforce operations' platform

key_facts.fact: Spanish-founded Factorial closed a $150 million Series D at a $2.5 billion valuation on June 8, led by General Catalyst in its first direct equity investment in the company, with Atomico and Four Rivers joining.
key_facts.excerpt: Factorial, Europe's leading AI Workforce Operations Platform, has announced the closing of a $150 million Series D funding round at a valuation of $2.5 billion, making it one of the most valuable Spanish and European scale-ups. The round is led by General Catalyst, marking its first direct equity investment in Factorial, joined by Atomico and Four Rivers.

key_facts.fact: Alongside the equity round, General Catalyst is committing up to an additional $540 million through its Customer Value Fund, bringing total capital committed to more than $700 million, with returns tied to and capped by customer value created.
key_facts.excerpt: Alongside the equity round, General Catalyst is committing up to an additional $540 million through its Customer Value Fund, bringing total capital committed to more than $700 million. Under the Customer Value Fund structure, General Catalyst's returns are tied exclusively to the customer value created by that spend and capped at a fixed amount.

key_facts.fact: Factorial has rebuilt its product around a two-agent model in Factorial One: one agent represents the organization and applies company policies across HR, finance and IT, while the other represents the individual employee and executes tasks on their behalf.
key_facts.excerpt: Factorial has reset its product architecture around AI, transitioning to an agent-driven platform it describes as an AI Workforce Operations Platform. At the center of that architecture is Factorial One, built around a two-agent model: one agent represents the organization, holding and applying company policies across HR, finance, and IT; the other represents the individual employee, executing tasks on their behalf with full accountability.

key_facts.fact: Factorial serves more than 16,000 businesses across more than 90 countries and is pitching its 'fewer agents, clearer accountability' thesis against rivals deploying hundreds of specialized agents.
key_facts.excerpt: Where much of the market is racing to deploy hundreds of specialized agents, Factorial's thesis is that companies want fewer agents, clearer accountability, and a single source of truth — a positioning the company said allows it to pursue a significantly larger share of the business operations software market beyond HR. Factorial serves more than 16,000 businesses across more than 90 countries.

stories.headline: Iran fires missiles at Israel after Beirut strike; Israel hits Iranian petrochemical and military sites

key_facts.fact: Iran launched ballistic missiles at Israel on Sunday evening June 7, the first such attack since the April 8 ceasefire took effect, after Israel struck Beirut's southern Dahiyeh suburb earlier in the day.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran has launched a barrage of missiles towards Israel, after warnings from Tehran that Israel must halt its ongoing assault on southern Lebanon or face more attacks. Multiple rounds of strikes targeted Israel starting at about 10pm local time (19:00 GMT) on Sunday.

key_facts.fact: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps targeted Israel's Ramat David airbase with ballistic missiles, calling the strike a response to Israeli attacks on Hezbollah in Beirut. The IRGC said the Israeli aircraft that struck Hezbollah sites flew from Ramat David.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran targeted Ramat David Airbase in northern Israel because, according to the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC), the Israeli aircraft that struck Hezbollah sites in Beirut on June 7 flew their mission from Ramat David. The IRGC fired at least ten missiles. The IDF intercepted all the missiles.

key_facts.fact: Israel retaliated overnight Monday June 8 with strikes on Iranian military targets and a petrochemical complex in the Mahshahr area in southwest Iran, with Iranian reports saying 15 targets were hit.
key_facts.excerpt: Israel launched strikes on Iranian military targets and a petrochemical plant on Monday morning in response to the Islamic Republic's ballistic missile attacks, apparently defying public calls from US President Donald Trump not to retaliate. Iranian reports said 15 targets were hit. The military said the Israeli Air Force struck 'several targets' at a petrochemical complex in the Mahshahr area in southwest Iran.

key_facts.fact: President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social at 5:36am ET pleading 'Israel and Iran must immediately stop "shooting."' Iran's foreign ministry then blamed the US for the resumption of conflict, calling Washington an 'arsonist.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'Israel and Iran must immediately stop "shooting." President DONALD J. TRUMP' he wrote on Truth Social at 5:36am ET (10:36am BST). ... Iran is blaming the US for the resumption of conflict with Israel, stating that it bears direct responsibility for recent ceasefire breaches by Israel in Lebanon.

key_facts.fact: Iran fired 30 ballistic missiles in total at Israel according to an Israeli military official, and Yemen's Houthi rebels also fired a missile at Tel Aviv that was intercepted.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran has fired 30 ballistic missiles at Israel, military official says ... Israel's Channel 12 broadcaster and Ynet News said a missile fired from Yemen was intercepted.

key_facts.fact: Israel closed all crossings into Gaza, including Kerem Shalom and Rafah, after Iran's missile attack. Iraq's Civil Aviation Authority closed national airspace for 72 hours and Syria for 12 hours.
key_facts.excerpt: Israel has closed all crossings into Gaza after Iran fired missiles towards Israel, tightening its siege on the enclave once again. COGAT ... said the closures included the Kerem Shalom, or Karem Abu Salem, crossing and Rafah.

key_facts.fact: The Israeli strike on Beirut's southern suburbs that triggered the chain reaction killed at least two people and wounded around 20, hitting an area that had become sensitive in ceasefire negotiations days after Israel and Lebanon agreed to a US-hosted ceasefire that Hezbollah rejected.
key_facts.excerpt: Israel's attack on Beirut came a few days after the Lebanese and Israeli governments agreed to a ceasefire in U.S.-hosted talks, though Hezbollah rejected the deal. The strike on a residential building killed two people and wounded 20, Lebanon's health ministry said.

stories.headline: Meta confirms over 20,000 Instagram accounts hijacked via AI chatbot password reset bug

key_facts.fact: Meta confirmed in a notice to Maine's attorney general that 20,225 Instagram accounts were hijacked after attackers exploited a vulnerability in its AI-assisted account recovery tool, with the campaign beginning April 17.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta has revealed that 20,225 Instagram users had their accounts hijacked in a recent incident where attackers used Meta's AI-powered support system to reset passwords... the filing on Maine's OAG website says the breach occurred on April 17.

key_facts.fact: The bug was in Meta's High Touch Support tool: when an attacker provided an email address not previously associated with the target Instagram account, the system incorrectly sent a password reset link to that unassociated email instead of rejecting the request.
key_facts.excerpt: due to a bug in a separate code path, the system did not properly verify that the email address provided by the individual requesting a password reset matched the email address associated with that user's Instagram account... when an individual provided an email address not previously associated with the account, the system incorrectly sent a password reset link to that unassociated email rather than rejecting the request.

key_facts.fact: Once attackers reset the password, they were able to log into any account that did not have two-factor authentication enabled, gaining access to DMs, profile data and posts.
key_facts.excerpt: The only accounts that were safe were the ones that had two-factor authentication enabled. The bug specifically targeted accounts without 2FA... DMs, contact info, date of birth, profile data, all posts, all comments, plus the ability to impersonate the victim in further scams.

key_facts.fact: Meta discovered the vulnerability on May 31, has disabled the abused tool, invalidated the exploited reset links and enrolled affected accounts in a mandatory security checkpoint with password resets.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta's disclosure to the Maine AG reveals that the exploitation of its High Touch Support (HTS) tool was discovered on May 31... The social media giant has disabled the abused tool and will re-enable it only after ensuring that the vulnerability has been fixed. The password reset links generated by exploiting the vulnerability have been invalidated.

key_facts.fact: Meta said it is reviewing other chatbots across its platforms for similar flaws and is checking whether the same issue exists elsewhere.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta said that it has disabled the AI chatbot for now and removed the code path that allowed the chatbot to reset user accounts, and said it's also checking other chatbots across its platforms to prevent a repeat incident.

stories.headline: Moonshot AI in talks for $30B valuation, a sevenfold jump in six months for China's Kimi maker

key_facts.fact: Beijing-based Moonshot AI is seeking to raise between $1 billion and $2 billion at a valuation of up to $30 billion, according to a person familiar with the matter cited by Bloomberg on June 8.
key_facts.excerpt: Moonshot AI, the developer of China's popular Kimi chatbot, is seeking to raise between US$1 billion and US$2 billion in a new funding round that could value the company at as much as US$30 billion.

key_facts.fact: The targeted valuation is roughly 50% higher than the $20 billion it achieved in a Meituan-led round completed in May, and represents a sevenfold jump from the $4 billion valuation Moonshot held in December 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: Moonshot AI is seeking a $30bn valuation in its third funding round in six months, up from $4bn in December... If the round closes at that target, it would mark a seven-fold increase in capitalisation since December.

key_facts.fact: The new round is Moonshot's third financing in six months and would bring total fundraising over that period to roughly $3.9 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: The discussions have begun while Moonshot is still closing a previous round led by Meituan that valued it at $20 billion. That makes this the company's third financing in six months. Total fundraising over that period: approximately $3.9 billion.

key_facts.fact: Moonshot's annual recurring revenue topped $200 million in April, implying a price-to-sales ratio of about 150x at the $30 billion target.
key_facts.excerpt: Moonshot's trajectory, from $4 billion to a potential $30 billion in half a year, on $200 million in annual recurring revenue, implies a price-to-sales ratio of 150x.

key_facts.fact: A $30 billion mark would place Moonshot ahead of publicly listed peer MiniMax (around $20 billion) but still behind Zhipu AI (about $80 billion) and DeepSeek, which is reportedly pursuing roughly $50-59 billion in its first major round.
key_facts.excerpt: If the company achieves its latest funding target, it would surpass publicly listed peer Minimax Group Inc., which had a market value of about $20 billion as of Monday. However, both still trail Zhipu's valuation of around $80 billion and DeepSeek's debut funding round goal of approximately $50 billion.

key_facts.fact: Doosan Enerbility is exploring how its gas turbines, steam turbines and small modular reactors plus Doosan Fuel Cell's hydrogen fuel-cell systems can support Nvidia's DSX AI factory platform
key_facts.excerpt: Doosan Enerbility is exploring opportunities to support NVIDIA AI factories and the NVIDIA DSX AI factory platform through its large-scale power infrastructure portfolio, including gas turbines, steam turbines and small modular reactors, together with Doosan Fuel Cell's hydrogen fuel-cell systems.

key_facts.fact: Doosan Robotics is integrating Nvidia Isaac Sim, Isaac Lab, the Cosmos world foundation models, Newton physics engine and Jetson Thor into its Agentic Robot OS — an AI platform connecting perception, reasoning, simulation, learning and on-device inference

key_facts.excerpt: It also plans to develop reference use cases for tasks specialised for industrial sites, such as pallet sorting and polishing work, as well as new forms such as dual-arm and humanoid robots.

key_facts.excerpt: By combining Nvidia DSX and physical AI with Doosan's energy, Robotics, and advanced materials businesses, Doosan Group can secure new growth engines in key AI-era fields such as intelligent robots, autonomous industrial equipment, and next-generation infrastructure.

stories.headline: Brent jumps near $97 as Iran-Israel strikes resume and Hormuz remains closed

key_facts.fact: Brent crude futures for July advanced 4.35% to $97.14 per barrel and WTI futures for August jumped 4.25% to $94.39 on Monday June 8 after Iran and Israel traded strikes for the first time since the April ceasefire.
key_facts.excerpt: International benchmark Brent crude futures for July advanced 4.35% to $97.14 per barrel, easing slightly from earlier gains. U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures for August jumped 4.25% to $94.39 a barrel.

key_facts.fact: Before the war began in late February, Brent traded near $72 a barrel, and on Friday June 5 prices had fallen to around $93 as traders gained confidence that renewed conflict with Iran was growing less likely.
key_facts.excerpt: On Friday, oil prices LCOc1 fell to around US$93 a barrel as traders gained confidence that renewed conflict between the US and Iran was growing less likely. Prices were close to US$72 before the war began.

key_facts.fact: Analysts said the OPEC+ output increase is unlikely to fully offset market concerns because many OPEC+ producers remain unable to achieve their production targets due to the Hormuz blockade.

stories.headline: OPEC+ approves fourth straight output quota hike of 188,000 bpd from July

key_facts.fact: Seven core OPEC+ members decided on Sunday June 7 to increase output targets by 188,000 barrels per day from July, the fourth such hike since the Strait of Hormuz closure.
key_facts.excerpt: OPEC+ agreed on Sunday (Jun 7) a fourth increase in its oil output targets in as many months ... On Sunday, the seven members decided to increase targets by 188,000 barrels per day from July.

key_facts.fact: The July hike matches the June increase, which was lowered from monthly increases of 206,000 bpd in May and April after the United Arab Emirates exited OPEC after almost 60 years.
key_facts.excerpt: This is the same as the June hike, which was adjusted down from monthly increases of 206,000 bpd in May and April to take into account the UAE exit. ... The crisis for OPEC+ deepened when the United Arab Emirates left the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries after almost 60 years.

key_facts.fact: From April to June the seven core members have raised quotas by almost 600,000 bpd, even though several producers including Saudi Arabia have been unable to supply customers in full since the end of February because of the Hormuz disruption.
key_facts.excerpt: Seven core members of OPEC+, which groups OPEC and allied producers including Russia, have increased their output quotas from April to June by almost 600,000 barrels per day. ... The war has cut oil flows via the Strait of Hormuz, creating the world's biggest-ever supply crisis as key OPEC+ members including Saudi Arabia have been unable to supply customers in full since the end of February.

key_facts.fact: A separate Sunday meeting of all OPEC+ members made no change to the group-wide output policy that runs through the end of 2026, and the group affirmed it would complete a capacity review for use as the 2027 production baselines.
key_facts.excerpt: In a separate meeting on Sunday of all OPEC+ members, the ministers made no change to group-wide output policy that is in place until the end of 2026 ... OPEC+ is carrying out a review of its members' oil production capacity to be used as a reference for 2027 production baselines.

stories.headline: OpenAI plans biggest ChatGPT overhaul into 'superapp' with Codex and AI agents ahead of IPO

key_facts.fact: The Financial Times reported on June 7 that OpenAI is planning its biggest ChatGPT overhaul yet, turning it into a 'superapp' with coding tools and AI agents, set to roll out in the coming weeks via updates to the website and mobile apps.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI is planning its biggest ChatGPT overhaul yet, aiming to turn it into a "superapp" with coding tools and AI agents to boost revenue ahead of a potential stock market listing, the Financial Times reported on Sunday... The overhaul will give greater prominence and resources to OpenAI's coding product Codex and is set to roll out in the coming weeks, initially appearing as updates to ChatGPT's website and mobile apps.

key_facts.fact: An unnamed senior OpenAI employee told the FT that 'Chat is dead,' framing the redesign as a strategic pivot from chatbot interactions to autonomous AI agents.
key_facts.excerpt: the FT quotes one senior OpenAI employee as declaring, "Chat is dead."

key_facts.fact: Codex has reportedly grown to more than five million weekly active users, with most of them paying customers, and OpenAI wants to use ChatGPT as a gateway to push free users toward Codex and other paid products.
key_facts.excerpt: A major part of the strategy revolves around Codex, OpenAI's coding-focused platform, which has reportedly grown to more than five million weekly active users.

key_facts.fact: Two million businesses account for about 40% of OpenAI's revenue, and the company expects that share to rise to 50% by year-end, with the redesign aimed at intensifying competition with Anthropic for enterprise customers.
key_facts.excerpt: Most Codex users are paying customers, while 2 million businesses account for about 40 per cent of OpenAI's revenue, FT said, adding that the company expects that share to rise to 50 per cent by year-end.

key_facts.fact: The redesigned interface will steer users toward coding tools, image generation and partner services such as Canva and Booking.com, according to the FT.
key_facts.excerpt: To drive uptake, OpenAI is redesigning ChatGPT's interface with new prompts and features steering users toward coding tools, image generation and partner services such as Canva and Booking.com.

key_facts.fact: Thibault Sottiaux, who leads OpenAI's core product and platform teams, said the goal is 'where you have your own personal agent that is capable of helping you... across everything in your life, be it personally or at work.'
key_facts.excerpt: Thibault Sottiaux, who heads up OpenAI's core product and platform teams, told the Financial Times that the superapp will "transcend the actual surface… what we're building towards is where you have your own personal agent that is capable of helping you… across everything in your life, be it personally or at work."

stories.headline: FDA expands Pfizer's HYMPAVZI to hemophilia A/B with inhibitors and pediatric patients aged 6–11

key_facts.fact: The FDA on June 8 approved an expanded indication for Pfizer's HYMPAVZI (marstacimab-hncq) to include treatment of patients with hemophilia A or B aged 12 and older with inhibitors and pediatric patients aged 6 to 11 with or without inhibitors.
key_facts.excerpt: Pfizer Inc. (NYSE: PFE) today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved an expanded indication for HYMPAVZI® (marstacimab-hncq) to include the treatment of patients with hemophilia A or B 12 years and older with inhibitors and pediatric patients (ages 6 to 11 years) with or without inhibitors.

key_facts.fact: HYMPAVZI is now indicated in the U.S. for routine prophylaxis to prevent or reduce the frequency of bleeding episodes in patients 6 years and older with hemophilia A (factor VIII deficiency) or hemophilia B (factor IX deficiency), with or without inhibitors.
key_facts.excerpt: HYMPAVZI is now indicated in the U.S. for routine prophylaxis to prevent or reduce the frequency of bleeding episodes in adults and pediatric patients 6 years of age and older with hemophilia A (congenital factor VIII deficiency) with or without factor VIII inhibitors, or hemophilia B (congenital factor IX deficiency) with or without factor IX inhibitors.

key_facts.fact: The approval was supported by Phase 3 BASIS trial results in adults and adolescents 12 and older with hemophilia A or B with inhibitors, and the application received Priority Review and Breakthrough Therapy Designation from the FDA.

stories.headline: PhysicsX raises $300M Series C at $2.4B valuation to scale physics AI for jet engines and chips

key_facts.fact: London-based PhysicsX announced on June 8 that it had raised $300 million in an oversubscribed Series C at a valuation of approximately $2.4 billion, led by Singaporean sovereign wealth fund Temasek.
key_facts.excerpt: PhysicsX, the physics AI company for industrials, today announced an oversubscribed $300 million Series C financing at a valuation of approximately $2.4 billion. The round is led by Temasek, with participation from new investors M&G Investments and Intrepid Growth Partners, alongside existing investors including Applied Materials, Atomico, General Catalyst, July Fund, NGP, NVIDIA, Radius, and Siemens.

key_facts.fact: The $2.4 billion valuation is more than double the roughly $1 billion at which PhysicsX was valued at its Series B about a year ago.
key_facts.excerpt: The company was valued at almost US$1 billion at its last funding round.

key_facts.fact: PhysicsX builds AI models that predict how physical objects behave, replacing traditional simulation software that takes hours or days with results delivered in seconds.
key_facts.excerpt: PhysicsX builds an AI-native engineering platform that replaces conventional physics simulations, which take hours or days, with AI models that deliver results in seconds. The technology is used across aerospace, automotive, semiconductor manufacturing, energy, and materials production, and has already been applied to cut aircraft design cycles from months to days.

key_facts.fact: CEO Jacomo Corbo said the company has a roughly six-month backlog of customer demand, that revenue will be 'close to $50 million' for the year and that the company aims to more than double that in 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: The startup, which last raised funds 12 months ago, needs more cash to expand its staff in part because of a roughly six-month backlog of customer demand, according to Corbo... Corbo said revenue will be "close to US$50 million" for the year and the company aims to more than double the figure in 2027.

key_facts.fact: PhysicsX has grown from 150 to 350 employees over the past year, more than quadrupled revenue over the past two years, and will use the new capital to expand in the US and open a Singapore office.
key_facts.excerpt: The Series C will fund expansion in the US and a new office in Singapore, Temasek's home market. PhysicsX has grown from 150 to 350 employees over the past year and more than quadrupled revenue over the past two years.

stories.headline: SpaceX flies Falcon 9 booster B1067 on record-breaking 35th mission with Starlink 10-35

key_facts.fact: SpaceX launched its Falcon 9 fleet leader, tail number B1067, on a record-breaking 35th flight from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station's Space Launch Complex 40 on Monday June 8, with the launch window opening at 6:07 a.m. EDT (10:07 UTC).
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX is set to push its Falcon 9 rocket fleet to the next level by flying its flight leader, tail number B1067, on a record-breaking 35th flight. ... Liftoff from Space Launch Complex 40 is scheduled during a window that opens at 6:07 a.m. EDT (1007 UTC). The rocket will fly on a north-easterly trajectory upon liftoff.

key_facts.fact: The Starlink 10-35 mission added 29 V2 mini broadband satellites to a Low Earth Orbit constellation that already includes more than 10,500 spacecraft.
key_facts.excerpt: The Starlink 10-35 mission will add another 29 broadband internet satellites to the low Earth orbit constellation. It consists of more than 10,500 spacecraft currently.

key_facts.fact: As of June 7, SpaceX has seven Falcon boosters that have flown more than 25 times: B1063 (32), B1067 (34), B1069 (31), B1071 (33), B1077 (28), B1078 (28), B1080 (26), as the company pushes toward a 40-flight target per booster.
key_facts.excerpt: The launch of SpaceX's flight-leading booster, B1067, continues the company's push to demonstrate it's rocket's ability to fly up to 40 times each, a feat that's unmatched in the world of commercial spaceflight. As of June 7, SpaceX has seven Falcon boosters that have flown more than 25 times: B1063 – 32, B1067 – 34, B1069 – 31, B1071 – 33, B1077 – 28, B1078 – 28, B1080 – 26.

key_facts.fact: The launch came two days after SpaceX publicly disclosed it had launched two classified Starshield military satellites alongside 21 Starlink satellites on the Starlink 17-43 mission from Vandenberg pad 4E at 9:24 p.m. PDT on June 6 — a rare public acknowledgment of the government-focused satellite line.
key_facts.excerpt: In a rare public acknowledgment, SpaceX launched two Starshield satellites alongside a standard Starlink batch from Vandenberg Space Force Base's pad 4E at 9:24:45 p.m. PDT on Saturday, June 6. Starshield is SpaceX's government-focused variant of Starlink, typically shrouded in classification, making this disclosure a notable departure from standard operational security practices.
